projects.title: Active Authentication
projects.description: Several years of research and development on a behavioral bio-metric continuous authentication program have culminated in the release of a Windows application. The Active Authentication application was developed at Louisiana Tech University by several student workers, a researcher, and an independent contractor as part of a DARPA research grant. The purpose of the Active Authentication system is to protect your system from access by unauthorized individuals. The system works by comparing the typing behavior of the individual currently using the computer to the stored profile of the computer's owner (or profiles of other authorized users). When suspicious typing behavior is detected further access to the computer is blocked until a one time password, sent to the owner's registered mobile phone and email account, is entered. The program is a pre-alpha open source release to SourceForge.

projects.title: CSC 404 / 403 Capstone Project
projects.description: Our capstone class was assigned with the task of building a web application to streamline the advising process for students and advisors in the Computer Science and Cyber Engineering department at Louisiana Tech University. The first 3 months (CSC 403 class) consisted primarily of initial planning, requirements gathering, and documentation generation. Starting in March, the class of CSC 404 began constructing the web application using various technologies including: MySQL, PHP, Code Igniter, jQuery. We used git / GitHub for change management and Trello for Agile methodology progress tracking. We deployed a testing / integration server that reflects our code on GitHub using Amazon's AWS cloud computing platform.
